node-17.label: Breast apocrine carcinoma (invasive carcinoma with apocrine differentiation)

attrs.why: This refines the broad frontier 'breast malignancy (carcinoma)' using the core needle biopsy showing carcinoma and immunohistochemistry positive for GCDFP-15, SOX10, S100, AR, with Ki-67 ~40%. These markers are characteristic of apocrine carcinoma, and both pathologist and radiologist interpretations favor this subtype. Surgical excision pathology is still needed for definitive subtyping and staging.

node-18.label: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST) with apocrine features

attrs.why: Invasive ductal carcinoma NST is the most common breast malignancy and can show focal apocrine features. However, the strong and diffuse apocrine marker profile (GCDFP-15, AR, SOX10, S100) makes pure NST less likely, though it remains a possible differential subtype within the carcinoma frontier.

Invasive lobular carcinoma can present as a palpable mass, but the immunohistochemistry shows positive E-Cadherin (node-13), which is typically lost or reduced in lobular carcinoma. This argues against lobular carcinoma and makes it an unlikely refinement of the current breast carcinoma frontier.

node-20.label: Other special subtype of breast carcinoma (e.g., metaplastic or secretory carcinoma)

attrs.why: S100 and SOX10 positivity can be seen in some special breast carcinoma subtypes such as metaplastic or salivary-gland-like tumors. However, the additional GCDFP-15 and AR positivity strongly favor apocrine differentiation, so other special subtypes remain only a low-probability refinement pending surgical excision pathology.
